Did Not Finish (DNF): DNF is the designation given when a runner does not complete the course
due to injury, violation of regulations, at the insistence of race staff or any other reason.
Did Not Start (DNS): DNS is the designation given when a runner decides not to complete the
course before passing the start line.
Disqualified (DSQ): When a runner is disqualified from the race.
GPX File: A type of GPS file that contains course information and maps that may be viewed on
mobile or watch devices
4. Standards for Operations and Decision-making
The race will begin at a predetermined place and time, and participants must move along the course
with only their own body, as in by running or walking, and follow the entire course within the
designated race duration until reaching the finish line.
Participants will be selected for awards based on their arrival time and according to race distance
category and gender division.
1) The first ranking is determined on-site by the referee and judges of the competition, and the
ranking is fixed unless there are any objections raised by other participants or the organizing
committee before the awards ceremony.
2) When an objection is raised, the objector must present clear evidence and/or witnesses for the
reason of objection, and if the objection is recognized, the ranking may change.
5. Eligibility
Participants must be physically healthy adults aged 18 or older on the day of the competition.
Minors may participate in certain race categories with the consent of a legal guardian. Participants
with health issues diagnosed by a professional medical institution or who are deemed unable to
participate will not be allowed to compete. Participants are solely responsible for any accidents or
disadvantages that occur during their participation in violation of these rules.
The race organizer has the right to request records of previous trail running races to assess
eligibility for certain race distances and difficulty. Failure to submit these records will result in
disqualification from participation.
6. Basic Requirements for Participation
1) Participant Agreement form (#Attachment 1.) in which participants agree to abide by the rules
and regulations related to this trail running event.
2) The participation fee must be paid to the designated bank account within the registration
deadline. Refunds must be requested as well within this deadline. Once this deadline has passed, no
changes may be made to registration.
3) Transferring of race bibs for any reason is strictly prohibited. Those who are found to be wearing
a bib that does not match the person who registered will be disqualified.
4) Participants are given the right to attend the race and receive all related benefits (souvenirs,
awards, etc.). If unable to attend due to personal reasons, registered participants may designate
another participant to receive their souvenir or apply for collection according to the procedure of the
race organizer within the designated period.

SEOUL ULTRA RALLY
Race Regulations
The following regulations apply to the trail running event hosted by Seoul Ultra Rally. Participants
must understand and strictly follow these regulations.
1. Race Organizing Committee
The race organizing committee is formed with the following members whose duty it is to facilitate a
safe and well-functioning event.
President: Race directing
Head of Operations: Employee dedicated to the operation of the race event
Head of Promotion: Employee dedicated to promotion of the event and securing partnerships
Timing Judge: Employee dedicated to the overall management of race start and finish timing,
participant records, and ranking.
Other positions determined by President: Operations personnel who cover additional needs related
to event management
2. Race Description and Distance Categories
Seoul Ultra Rally defines "trail running" as a type of running event that takes place primarily in
mountainous terrain, including well-maintained and unmaintained hiking trails, official park trails
(dulegil), gravel roads, and connecting urban paved roads or pedestrian walkways that are
designated as part of the running course by the race organizer.
3. Key Terms
Understanding the following terms is necessary for participants to fully understand related
information and announcements before and during the race. The following terms are used generally
in all international trail races.
Cut-off Time: The time by which runners must arrive to continue with the race. Runners who do not
arrive by cut-off time are disqualified.
Marking: Temporary signs, ribbons, or other markings that provide information to runners on the
course direction.
Check Point (CP): Points along the course where runners/participants have time checks, can assess
their physical condition, and refuel. All runners are required to pass through the check points, and
those who miss the check points will be disqualified.
Course Marshal/Volunteer/Medical Staff: A course marshal, volunteer, or medical staff is any
person who is tasked with providing course directions, traffic control, marking, or emergency
response services for the runners during the duration of the race.
Sweeper: The sweeper is a volunteer who runs alongside the final runners within the cut-off time, or
who prevents those who have exceeded cut-off time from continuing. Any runners who remain
behind the sweeper are automatically disqualified.

Participants are responsible for checking notices from the race organizer via the organizer website,
group chat, or social media. Participants are responsible for familiarizing themselves with the race
day information, regulations, and GPX files (course maps).
7. Required Gear
Runners must come prepared with the required gear specified by the race organizer according to
their race distance and difficulty level. Failure to wear or carry the required items will result in
inability to participate, disqualification, or time penalties.
Gear checks may be conducted at any time before, during, or after the race.
*The required gear is listed in #Appendix2.
8. Reasons for Disqualification
1) Failure to register within the designated period or failure to submit the participation consent and
agreement form.
2) Not wearing one's assigned bib or wearing someone else's bib.
3) Causing damage to course marking or signs prepared by the race organizer.
4) Deviating from the course, taking shortcuts, or not passing through checkpoints (CPs).
5) Interfering with the performance of other participants.
6) Engaging in verbal abuse, swearing, shouting, or other unsportsmanlike behaviors during the
race.
7) Non-compliance with instructions of race officials or staff.
8) Decision to stop race progress before or during the race.
9) Violation of traffic regulations on road sections.
10) Using any other form of transportation besides running or walking.
11) Utilizing outside crews or undesignated supply locations. Only official checkpoints may be
utilized.
12) Littering or damage to the natural environment at any point of the course.
13) Positive result of doping test.
14) Violation of other grounds for disqualification that are determined by the race organizer.
*Participants who receive serious violations may be prohibited from participating in future races.
9. Safety and Injury Prevention
Participants are solely responsible for avoiding injury and responding to accidents that may occur
during the race.
The following procedure should be followed in case of injury.
1) Call the emergency contact number listed on the bib.
2) If the emergency contact is unavailable, contact emergency services at 119.
3) Make your situation known to other participants or race staff so that they may communicate
your need for assistance to the race organizers.
4) If possible, make your way to the nearest CP or urban area.
5) Use your first aid kit (items listed under required gear) to provide yourself with any emergency
care needed while waiting for assistance.
